transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because I keep getting stuck on worries. It can be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work. Once it starts, I can’t seem to put it away in my mind, even if I make lists or try to redirect myself.
When these worries get stuck in your mind, do you find yourself doing any repeated checking or mental rituals to feel less anxious?

I’m not sure I’d call it rituals. I do check things sometimes, like if I’m worried I missed something, but it’s more that I keep thinking it through over and over. I don’t have a specific routine I have to do to make it feel okay.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life, rather than mainly one specific problem?

Yes, it’s definitely not just one thing anymore. Over the past year it started with worrying about my mother’s safety, but now it spreads to finances, decisions with staff, deadlines, things around the house, whether I’m being a good daughter… even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worrying?

Yes. Once it starts, it’s really hard to stop. I can make lists or try to focus on something else, but the worry just keeps circling in my mind—whether it’s about my mother, a work report, or something I think I may have missed. It doesn’t feel like I can just set it aside.
Do these thoughts ever feel intrusive or unwanted in a way that seems irrational or out of proportion, rather than like ordinary worries about real-life problems?

I’m not sure. They feel unwanted because I don’t want to be thinking about them all the time, but they don’t usually feel bizarre or completely irrational. They’re mostly about real things—I just think I take them too far and can’t let them go.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d say depressed most days. I’ve felt stressed and worn down, but not really down in that way, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge much of the time?
I’m not really sure. I do feel keyed up sometimes, but I haven’t been paying attention to whether it’s most of the time or just when I’m worried about something.
Has this kind of hard-to-control worrying been happening more days than not for at least six months?
Yes. It’s been more days than not, I’d say. It started around when my mother moved in with me after her fall, and that was about a year and two months ago.
Do you often feel muscle tension, like your shoulders, neck, or jaw staying tight?

Yes, I do. By the end of the day my neck and shoulders feel really tight, like I’ve been bracing myself without noticing. And I catch myself clenching my jaw a lot, especially when I’m answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes. Most nights I have trouble falling asleep because I’m lying there going over the day or trying to plan for everything that could go wrong. And if I wake up because I hear my mother moving around, I’m usually awake for another hour or two after that. Then I go into work at the library feeling like I never really rested.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yes. At work especially, during cataloging reviews or staff meetings, I’ll be looking right at the screen or the agenda and then realize I haven’t taken in any of it. My mind has gone off into some problem I feel like I should have prevented, and I have to reread things or ask myself what I just missed.
Have these worries been interfering with your day-to-day life?

Yes, it has. At the library I’ve started missing small but important details, things I normally would catch. And recently I froze during part of a grant presentation and had to hand some of it off to someone else. That’s really not like me, and it’s made me worry about whether I can keep leading my team the way I should.
Did these symptoms start after your mother moved in with you following her fall?
Yes. It started after she moved in with me after her fall. It’s been going on for about a year and two months now.
Do you feel your level of worry is out of proportion to what most people would feel about your mother living with you after her fall?

Yes, I think it is. I mean, of course anyone would worry about their mother after a fall, but mine doesn’t stay there. Over the past year it’s spread into worrying about money, decisions at work, deadlines, the house, whether I’m being a good daughter… even small things start to feel like they’re going to unravel.
